name: Sri Sithi Vinayagar Temple
significance: A Dravidian-style Ganesha temple on Jalan Selangor in Petaling Jaya, completed in 1964 and first consecrated that November. It is run by the Petaling Jaya Hindu Association, registered in 1959, and has been rebuilt and reconsecrated three times since, most recently in 2007.

name: Sri Sundararaja Perumal Temple
significance: A Vaishnava temple in the royal town of Klang dedicated to Vishnu as Perumal, built in 1892 and wholly reconstructed in 2015 as the first granite temple in Malaysia. Its gopuram carved with images of the deities has made it a principal Perumal shrine for Malaysian Tamils, who call it the Tirupati of Southeast Asia.

name: Seafield Sri Maha Mariamman Temple
significance: A Mariamman temple in the USJ suburb of Subang Jaya, believed but never proven to have been founded in 1891. Its forced relocation from land sold by Sime Darby to the One City developer MCT Bhd produced a long dispute that erupted into rioting in 2018, making it the best-known temple land case in Malaysia.

name: Sree Maha Mariamman Devasthanam Temple, Butterworth
significance: One of the oldest Hindu foundations on mainland Penang, established at Bagan Luar in Butterworth in 1853 and given a permanent temple by Ponnusami Pillai in 1903. The present Dravidian structure, whose gopuram towers over the surrounding buildings, was raised in the 1980s and consecrated in 1988.
story: The temple is said to have begun when an image of Ambal was found by the seaside in 1853 and a small hut was put up on the spot to shelter her for worship.

name: Maravijaya Buddha
significance: A 25 m marble image of the seated Buddha at Naypyidaw, cut from stone quarried at Sagyin near Mandalay. Work began on 14 June 2020 and the statue was consecrated on 1 August 2023, the project driven by the ruling State Administration Council and funded largely by military-linked businessmen and retired officers.
story: Its name Maravijaya means to conquer Mara, the demon the Buddha overcame at the moment of his enlightenment.

name: Win Sein Taw Ya
significance: A Theravada monastic site near Mudon in Mon State holding the world's largest free-standing reclining Buddha, 180 m long and 30 m tall. Work on the image began on 29 February 1992 under the founding monk Win Sein Sayadaw, and its hollow interior carries a multi-level museum of chambers depicting scenes from the Buddha's life.
